headline: Approved Boston Avenue zoning amendments, a public tree ordinance, and an $11,640.00 Sentry Ford settlement.
summary: The council approved the Boston Avenue zoning amendments on a second vote after reconsidering the first. It approved the Public Tree Ordinance 7-0 and an $8,500.00 Community Preservation appropriation for TreesMedford. It tabled the FY27 supplemental appropriation until September 29th.

Medford City Council 
Medford, Massachusetts 
  
The Fifteenth Regular Meeting, September 15, 2026 
 
This meeting took place in the City Council Chamber, 2nd Floor, Medford City Hall, 85 George 
P. Hassett Drive, Medford, MA and via Zoom. To submit written comments, please email 
REliseo@medford-ma.gov. 
 
CALL TO ORDER 
 
President Zac Bears called the Fifteenth Regular Meeting of the Medford City Council to order in 
the Council Chambers and via Zoom. 
 
ROLL CALL 
 
Present: President Bears; Vice President Lazzaro; Councilor Callahan; Councilor Leming; 
Councilor Mullane; Councilor Scarpelli; Councilor Tseng. Seven members were present and no 
members were absent. Inside the Rail: City Clerk Laurel Siegel.

26-148 - Resolution to Invite Residents to Ward 1 Neighborhood Meeting on September 
23rd 
Offered by Isaac Bears, Council President, Liz Mullane, City Councilor, Justin Tseng, City 
Councilor 
 
Be it Resolved by the Medford City Council that we invite the residents of Ward 1 to attend the 
Ward 1 Neighborhood Meeting on September 23rd at 7PM at the Andrews Middle School. This 
meeting will be hosted by Councilor Mullane and Councilor Tseng, and residents are welcome 
to attend and discuss improvements they would like to see in their neighborhood. 
 
For more information and for a Zoom link when it is available, please visit the City of Medford 
Events Calendar. 
 
Motion to approve by Councilor Mullane, seconded by Councilor Tseng. Approved on a Roll 
Call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed. 
 
26-153 - Resolution to Acknowledge and Celebrate National Recovery Month 
Offered by Emily Lazzaro, Council Vice President 
 
Whereas September is National Recovery Month; and 
 
Whereas harm reduction is under attack by the federal government and programs and services 
have been eliminated wholesale, which will most certainly result in overdoses and deaths; and 
 
Whereas Medford’s Department of Health and Human Services does powerful work every day 
to support our residents in recovery, now therefore: 
 
Be it hereby resolved that the Medford City Council acknowledge and celebrate National 
Recovery Month and continue to work publicly to push back against negative stigma regarding 
those in recovery, and celebrate their achievements and their inherent value. 
 
Addressing the Council: 
Jason Stone, Social Services Coordinator 
Chris Summa, Recovery Coach 
 
Motion to approve by Vice President Lazarro, seconded by Councilor Tseng. Approved on a 
Roll Call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed.
26-157 - Resolution in Memory of Lorraine Marie Miles 
Offered by George Scarpelli, City Councilor 
 
Be it RESOLVED, that the Medford City Council  extends its deepest condolences to former 
School Committee member Kathy Kreatz and the Miles family on the passing of her mother, 
Lorraine Marie Miles, a devoted Medford resident and educator, on August 21, 2026, and further 
resolves that a moment of silence be observed in her memory and a copy of this resolution be 
transmitted to the family. 
 
Motion to approve by Councilor Scarpelli, seconded by Councilor Mullane. Approved on a Roll 
Call vote of Seven in favor, Zero opposed. 
 
 
Records

them to be in order.

REFER TO COMMITTEE FOR FURTHER DISCUSSION 
 
26-154 - Resolution to Discuss Safety Improvements at the West Medford Train Station 
(to be referred to Public Health and Community Safety Committee)Offered by Emily 
Lazzaro, Council Vice President 
 
Whereas the West Medford train station is recognized by the Massachusetts Bay Transit 
Authority (the MBTA) as one of the most dangerous in the state, and; 
 
Whereas the MBTA knew the dangers associated with the West Medford at-grade crossing 
since at least 2023; and 
 
Whereas the MBTA had planned safety upgrades in the works since at least 2023; and 
 
Whereas the MBTA made ADA accessibility upgrades to the West Medford train station 
recently, but did not make the safety upgrades that would have significantly increased safety to 
the at-grade crossing; and 
 
Whereas John Westwater was injured by a train on July 20th and subsequently died from his 
injuries; and 
 
Whereas it is the duty of government agencies such as the MBTA and local leaders to be 
proactive in protecting residents, especially vulnerable residents such as seniors, people with 
disabilities, and children from known safety hazards, now therefore: 
 
Be it hereby resolved that the Medford City Council hold a meeting of the Public Health and 
Community Safety Committee to discuss the timeline of planned safety upgrades with the 
MBTA, also inviting our state delegation in order to have all interested and empowered parties 
in discussion publicly. 
 
Motion to approve by Vice President Lazarro, seconded by Councilor Tseng. Approved on a

26-156 - Resolution Calling for the Immediate Release of Medford Resident 
Vijay D’Souza from ICE Detention in Atlanta Offered by Matt Leming, City Councilor, Isaac 
Bears, Council President, Justin Tseng, City Councilor 
 
WHEREAS Vijay D’Souza, a Medford resident and longtime member of the First Baptist Church 
of Medford, was detained by ICE on a return flight to Boston in the Atlanta Airport on August 
29th, 2026; 
 
WHEREAS Mr. D’Souza had been actively working with an attorney on a green card application 
at the time of his detention; 
 
WHEREAS No information about the reasons for this detention were given to his wife, who has 
been working with an attorney on his release; 
 
WHEREAS This detention has caused a great deal of distress to Mr. D’Souza’s family, who
continues to fight for his release; the First Baptist Church of Medford, who spearheaded a letter-
writing campaign on his behalf; and the Medford community in general, who has been greatly 
distressed by the latest of many unlawful abductions by ICE in and around our community; 
 
BE IT RESOLVED that the Medford City Council offer the highest possible endorsement for the 
release of Mr. D’Souza and allow him to continue with his green card process; 
 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that we condemn these acts and recognize the continued harm 
and fear that they inflict on our city and country.

Section 94-9.8 BOSTON AVENUE NEIGHBORHOOD CORRIDOR DISTRICT 
94-9.8.1 Purpose 
The purpose of the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor District (BANCD) is to allow a mix 
of uses, including residential, multifamily, and commercial, to meet the following needs: 
1. Wider variety of uses and building types to support jobs and economic development near 
established residential neighborhoods, providing options for living within walking distance of 
jobs, goods, and services and the Green Line T stations. 
2. Fluid transitions to and from the Tufts University campus to allow an integrated approach to 
living working and learning along Boston Avenue from  the Somerville line north of Stoughton 
Street to the Somerville border at Ball Square. 
3. Mixed-use, multifamily, and commercial uses at a density to reinforce non-vehicular travel 
between the adjacent neighborhoods to the jobs, goods, and services within the BANCD. 
4. Development standards to provide landscape and height buffers from new construction within 
the BANCD for the existing abutting neighborhoods. 
94-9.8.2 Applicability 
The BANCD replaces the existing zoning districts and is shown on the Zoning Map, City of 
Medford, Massachusetts, as amended. An applicant may develop within these districts in 
accordance with the provisions of Section 94-9.8 and other relevant sections of the Zoning 
Ordinance. 
1. The BANCD is comprised of the following subdistricts: 
a. BA-1. This mixed-use subdistrict allows a mix of residential and commercial uses 
at a lower scale of building size and massing. 
b. BA-2. This mixed-use subdistrict allows a mix of residential and commercial uses 
at a medium scale of building size and massing.  
i. BA-2a. This subdistrict location and surrounding characteristics allow for 
greater growth and development. 
ii. BA-2b. This subdistrict has smaller-scale requirements to respond to its 
surroundings and provide a transition towards the residential neighborhoods. 
c. BA-3. This mixed-use subdistrict allows a mix of residential and commercial uses 
at a larger scale of building size and massing.

94-9.8.4 Dimensional Waivers. 
The following waivers are available to the Site Plan Review or Special Permit Granting 
Authority for projects within the BANCD, upon a finding that such waiver would not cause 
substantial detriment to the neighborhood.  
1. Height Exemption. The limitation on the height of buildings shall not apply to chimneys, 
ventilators, towers, silos, spires, or other ornamental features of buildings, which features 
are in no way used for living purposes and do not constitute more than twenty-five (25) 
percent of the ground floor area of the building. 
2. Height Waiver: Energy-Efficiency. The Site Plan Review Authority or Special Permit 
Granting Authority may waive the height and setbacks in 94-9.8.3 Dimensional Standards 
to accommodate the installation of any building system or equipment which conserves, 
reduces, or offsets the building energy use. Where feasible, mechanical components shall 
be placed as close to the center of the roof as possible. Such installations shall not create a 
significant detriment to abutters in terms of noise or shadow and shall be appropriately 
integrated into the architecture of the building and the layout of the site. The installations 
shall not provide additional habitable space within the development. 
3. Height Stepback Waiver. If a building is subject to a front stepback and rear or side 
stepbacks, the Community Development Board may waive the strict dimensional 
requirement of any of the stepbacks, provided that priority is given to retaining the 
stepback(s) in 94-9.8.3.2.c Height Transition to Adjacent Residential Districts. 
4. Setback Waiver: Drop-off zone. The required setback distances may be waived to allow 
for a cut-out along the curb for loading and short-term parking for deliveries or drop-
off/pick-up zones. Such a cut-out shall be coordinated with City staff.

Offered by Councilor Callahan 
 
Public Tree Preservation, Protection, and Replacement Ordinance 
 
Chapter 86, Article III, of the City of Medford Ordinances is hereby amended as follows: 
 
Section 86-91 hereby deleted in its entirety and the following new sections are hereby adopted: 
 
Sec. 86-91 - Intent and Purpose 
 
This ordinance is enacted for the purpose of preserving and protecting both Public Shade Trees 
and trees otherwise located on public property as set forth herein. 
 
The State Legislature has granted municipalities the right and responsibility to protect the 
health, safety, and welfare of their residents through the creation and enactment of regulations. 
Zoning powers further allow municipalities to “regulate the use of land, buildings and structures 
to the full extent of independent constitutional powers of cities and towns to protect the health, 
safety and general welfare of their present and future inhabitants,” according to MGL Chapter 
40A. 
 
A mature tree canopy protects the community in critically important ways. It reduces: energy 
consumption, ambient summertime temperatures, air pollution, flooding, and soil erosion. It 
provides privacy, absorbs noise, and boosts mental health. It supports wildlife and increases 
resilience to climate change. It also maintains the natural beauty of Medford for all to enjoy 
today and for future generations. Protecting the City’s tree canopy is thus an essential 
community function and public purpose. This protection requires the City to manage its urban 
forest. 
 
To achieve this purpose, this ordinance outlines the procedures that the Tree Warden will use to 
regulate the removal and replacement of public trees. This ordinance also establishes a Tree 
Fund to supplement the City budget for tree maintenance, tree planting, stump removal, and site 
preparation for tree planting on public land.
39 
 
 
Sec. 86-92 Urban Forest Management Plan 
 
The City shall maintain and periodically update the Urban Forest Management Plan to guide the 
preservation, maintenance, removal, replacement, and planting of Public Trees. 
The Tree Warden and relevant City departments shall consider and substantially follow the 
goals, priorities, and best practices identified in the Plan when making decisions regarding 
public tree management, tree replacement, species selection, stump removal, and planting 
priorities. 
The Plan shall promote the long-term health, diversity, resilience, and equitable distribution of 
the City’s urban forest. 
 
Sec. 86-93 - Definitions 
 
Caliper: Diameter of a tree trunk (in inches) measured 12 inches above the ground for trees up 
to and including eight inches in diameter. For larger trees, the diameter is measured 24 inches 
above the ground. 
 
Certified Arborist: A professional arborist possessing current certification issued by the 
International Society of Arboriculture (I.S.A.) and/or the Massachusetts Arborist Association 
(M.A.A.). 
 
Urban Forest Management Plan: Plan to identify the City's goals and priorities for managing 
its public trees; to describe the status of the City's urban forest resources and its management 
program; and to document the methods, resources, and personnel that will be used to achieve 
these goals over the next five years. 
 
Construction: Any activity that affects trees, tree root zones, or is within the drip line and that 
requires a building permit or trench permit, including driveways, retaining walls, solar installation 
where trees are removed, site work on foundations, underground utilities, excavation, grading, 
and paving construction or alteration of a structure or structures where the drip zone of a tree 
would be affected. 
 
Demolition: Any act of pulling down, destroying, removing or razing a building; or altering or 
disturbing the landscape, removing trees, soils or supporting vegetation; or commencing such 
work with the intent of completion. 
 
DBH ("Diameter at Breast Height"):  The tree diameter in inches measured at 4.5 feet above 
the ground. For multi-stemmed trees, the size is determined by measuring all the trunks, and 
then adding the total diameter of the largest trunk to one-half the diameter of each additional 
trunk.  
 
Drip Line: The area directly under the tree at the outer circumference of the tree branches, 
where most of the rainwater shed from the tree canopy drips to the ground. The Critical Root 
Zone (CRZ) lies within the drip line. 
 
Hazardous Trees: Any tree that has been deemed by the Tree Warden to be dead, injured, and 
dangerous, where the hazard cannot be eliminated by pruning. Any tree that is likely to cause 
disease or infestation in other trees; is in imminent danger of falling; is dangerously close to 
existing structures; is causing disruption of public utility service; is causing drainage or passage
40 
 
problems upon rights-of-way that cannot be remediated by other means; or that poses an 
unavoidable threat to pedestrian or vehicular safety that cannot be eliminated by pruning. 
 
Landmark Tree: Any healthy tree may be designated as a Landmark Tree if it meets one of 
more of the following criteria: a) a tree that is documented to be 50 years old or older; b) is 24 
inches in diameter or more at breast height; c) represents a rare species; d) is associated with a 
historical event or person, unusual feature, or scenic enhancement. All Landmark Trees are 
Protected Trees except those listed as invasive species on the Massachusetts Invasive Plants 
list. 
. 
Landscape Design Plan: A written description and scale drawing of the future site that 
includes the locations of plantings, structures, hardscape, greenscape, and topography, and 
indicates the future canopy. 
 
Medford Tree Committee: The Committee established to promote the planting and protection 
of trees in Medford. 
 
Person: Any Medford resident, property owner, firm, partnership, association, 
corporation, company or organization of any kind including public or private utility and municipal 
department. 
 
Protected Tree: All public trees as defined in this section except those listed as invasive

Public Tree: All trees within a public way, public park or its boundaries, or leased land being

of-way. (See G.L.c.87 s.1) 
Tree Fund: An account established pursuant to this ordinance for the deposit of payments for

Tree Removal:   Removal or destruction by saws, or other mechanical means of a living tree, or

Tree Removal Permit: Permit issued by the Tree Warden for removal of public trees based on

Tree Save Zone: The area surrounding all Protected Trees to the drip line, sufficiently large to

Tree Warden:  As defined in G.L. c.87 s.2 and Medford Rev. Ords. 1974, ch. 26, § 2, the Tree 
Warden is the City employee responsible for the management of the City’s public trees.  
 
Urban Forest: All of the Protected Trees in the City and the lands that support those trees.

Re: Change of definition of “Building Height” in Medford Zoning 
 
 
There was a question about when the definition of “Building Height” was changed during the 
City’s Zoning process. During the Medford Square public hearing in January, it became clear 
that there was a misunderstanding about how “height” (of a building) is measured in the City of 
Medford, with some people assuming that the measurement is made from the ground the 
building sits on, and others believing it was measured from the curb of the road the building 
faces. 
 
When it was clarified that the definition of building height in Medford Zoning was measured from 
the curb, and it was clarified that this was not a standard definition, but something unusual in 
Medford’s ordinances, the Council & CDB requested that the consultants provide a definition 
that is more standard, i.e., measuring from the land or “finished grade” that the building sits on, 
and for sloped land, the “average grade”.   
 
This definition was provided in the edits presented at the joint public hearing on March 25th, and 
was adopted as part of the vote on April 28, 2026.  When new or revised definitions are adopted 
as part of the zoning, they are always city-wide, and not for one district. This is to avoid long-
term confusion.  This is indicated by the table at the beginning of each zoning memo, where the 
portions of the zoning that are being amended are listed.  “Section 94-12.0. Definitions” is the 
section for definitions for the entire zoning document and is where that definition was included.
